original_value: The geostationary remote sensing satellite has the capability of wide scanning, persistent observation and operational response, and has tremendous potential for maritime target surveillance. The GF-4 satellite is the first geostationary orbit (GEO) optical remote sensing satellite with medium resolution in China. In this paper, a novel ship-tracking method in GF-4 satellite sequential imagery is proposed. The algorithm has three stages. First, a local visual saliency map based on local peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) is used to detect ships in a single frame of GF-4 satellite sequential images. Second, the accuracy positioning of each potential target is realized by a dynamic correction using the rational polynomial coefficients (RPCs) and automatic identification system (AIS) data of ships. Finally, an improved multiple hypotheses tracking (MHT) algorithm with amplitude information is used to track ships by further removing the false targets, and to estimate ships’ motion parameters. The algorithm has been tested using GF-4 sequential images and AIS data. The results of the experiment demonstrate that the algorithm achieves good tracking performance in GF-4 satellite sequential images and estimates the motion information of ships accurately.

result.paraphrase: Geostationary remote sensing satellites can perform wide-area scanning, continuous observation, and operational response, giving them strong potential for maritime target surveillance. GF-4 is China’s first medium-resolution optical remote sensing satellite in geostationary orbit (GEO). This paper presents a new ship-tracking approach for GF-4 sequential imagery. The method has three stages. First, ships are detected in a single GF-4 frame using a local visual saliency map based on local peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Second, each candidate target is precisely localized through dynamic correction with the satellite’s rational polynomial coefficients (RPCs) and ship automatic identification system (AIS) data. Finally, an enhanced multiple hypotheses tracking (MHT) algorithm incorporating amplitude information is used to track ships, eliminate false targets, and estimate their motion parameters. The algorithm was evaluated with GF-4 sequential images and AIS data, and the experimental results show that it provides strong tracking performance and accurately estimates ship motion information.
